claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as heavily reliant on trial and error, requiring players to restart entire levels after making a mistake.

citations.review_text: Poor controls when reaction time so important. Game artificially long due to restarting entire levels after a tiny error. Not a fun game. Very trial and error.

Did not enjoy the gameplay, played a lot of punishing games through the years but this was just unnecessarily stressful, couldn't keep playing after a few tries, the whole "bring you back to the beginning of each stage" is just not my thing and ends up being tedious, also relying so much on the slow down mechanic just breaks my rhythm playing, was just coming off of playing nine sols and  bo: path of the teal lotus, and loved those games,  so i wanted to keep on the metroid-vania genre, but this one just wasn't for me, I'm too old to have to invest so much time in just "getting good" when there's so many other options. Music, graphics and story (from what I've read), are great, the delivery, not for me.

Sure, the gameplay is pretty decent, pretty similar to a 2D Platformer take on the Hotline Miami formula--you kill in 1 hit and die in 1 hit (most of the time). It's up to your reaction speed, planning, and repeated attempts to nail down a strategy that will allow you to succeed at a level.

Something I did not expect out of this game was the incredible presentation on the story--I'd honestly rank that aspect as better and more interesting than the combat. The way the dialogue choice system works is honestly really interesting, you can choose to interrupt characters in the middle of them talking, and your options change the further into their dialogue they get before you speak. Sometimes, options that might seem to be better disappear if you wait too long, so it really incentivizes you to be decisive. This system compliments the games narrative really nicely, but I don't want to talk about that too much since it very quickly gets into spoiler territory. 

Definitely give this game a go if you enjoy fast paced gameplay, and subversive and interactive narrative experiences.

What we have so far? 10/10, easily.

The action, art, music, and overall style are just breathtaking. The game is fast paced, and just super well done. However:
The story is kind of hard to judge, this game ends on a cliffhanger, and the story right now has a lot of mysteries. So, it's incomplete so far. There's more planned content, but because this game is made by a small team, it likely won't be out for a bit. Just keep that in mind.

any day now.

This is a fun, bite-sized experience. Great on the Steam Deck, too. 

It wears its inspiration of HOTLINE MIAMI on its sleeves: you're going to die, a lot, but you'll learn something in each death. Reloads are quick, so there's not much of a sting. 

The aesthetics are great (like a 90's anime, almost), and the writing is particularly sharp. If I have a knock on it story-wise, it's that [spoiler] it's not a complete story. I genuinely cant believe it was only 5 hours, peak game and the story was suprisingly good, I thought it was going to be bad but it genuinely shocked me how the plot unfolded. A bit sad it ended on a cliff hanger though

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game's story ends on an unresolved cliffhanger, leaving players awaiting a promised downloadable content (DLC) expansion.

citations.review_text: GOAT, best game ever, 100/10 peak music, peak gameplay, peak visuals, great story, but where's dlc, i can't completely tell how good your story if you just never release it fully. Also try SANABI btw.

Smooth and fun gameplay. Memorable art style. Short, but good for replays. Runs on my potato laptop. Choices in the game are consequential, but they affect only minor occurrences but not the overall fate of the main characters. The plot and and the dialogue intertwine to create a believable and fascinating Cyberpunk world, but don't get your hopes high for the ending because it is a cliffhanger of which the completion depends on a DLC that people have been waiting for years.

A common comparison you'll hear is that Katana Zero is like if Hotline Miami was 2D, and it's definitely not an inaccurate one. It's just as difficult, but addicting, with a similarly dark and memorable story. It also similarly has a very unique artstyle to match one of the best soundtracks any indie game's ever had. All in all, it is an amazing game that is no question worth the fifteen dollars it's priced, despite being pretty short (about 4 hours, though granted, 100%ing takes a lot more time and is definitely worth doing for both personal achievement and small bonuses).

However, do know that going into it you will be playing what is effectively an unfinished game. It ends on an awful cliffhanger that's supposed to lead into a dlc fans have been waiting on for 7 years at the time of writing, a wait longer than the original game's development time, and has (also at the time of writing) no indication of being done soon. I think that it's worth playing through despite this, but any players should know that coming into the game that there's no guarantee it'll ever actually be finished.

[h1]Masterpiece[/h1]
Katana ZERO has the best synergy between gameplay features and story elements of any game ever made. The levels are masterfully crafted and introduce new elements at the right time to prevent the player from getting bored. The animations are smooth and responsive. The fast-paced gameplay is accompanied by a great soundtrack. The end of the game doesn't conclude the story, leaving the door open for future content.

[h1]My request to Justin Stander (Askiisoft)[/h1]
Whenever you conclude the story, please give me the option to save the little girl from those disgusting, creepy men in the masks. I told her: "I won't let anyone hurt you."

The story was great, i love that you can interrupt people mid conversation like “shut up” or “♥♥♥♥ you”, the art is very very good, and the animations are absolutely beautiful. I feel like there’s so much ♥♥♥♥ to talk about with this game but i really dont wanna spoil a single thing and you should just play it cuz it’s only 4 hours long. One of the most interesting stories I've experienced in a long time and the gameplay is phenomenal. On top of that the soundtrack is bumping and the art direction for the pixel art couldn't be better. Only complaint is the game is rlly short at roughly 4 hours long - but it does have a lot of replayability with the hard mode / speed run game modes.

[H1]You believe a man can change his destiny?[/H1]
Katana Zero... one of my favorite games. I replay it from time to time, and usually it ends up being a longplay. It REALLY has that replaybility thanks to non-linear dialogues and even executions of the scenes.
What do we have? A distopian cyberpunk. We're talking Akira stuff in here. You play as Zero, unnamed self-made samurai with ability to... predict how things will go, plan how you will get through, and get through. But who are you? How come you can do all this? What are you targets? WHY? WHY?!

[H2]Pros:[/H2]
-Fun fast-paced gameplay
-Great soundtrack
-Pretty good animations
-Great plot
-Replayability due to non-linear approach on both levels and dialogues
-Fun little gags here and there
-Pixelated violence that doesn't go off and can give you some Hotline Miami vibes of "You enjoy killing. That's why"

Will be interesting to pin-point some of cons... Let me try.
[H2]Cons[/H2]
-Slow-mo will most of the time make you useless
-The knockout is mostly certainly fatal
-Interesting usage of russian language that sometimes could be better
-Too vague to pin-point at least anything realistic going on. Maybe DLC will explain, but I doubt it.
-Secret boss-fight shouldn't be secret. It's the best ending of the story.

Overall, this game is perfect. It's challenging, it's fun, it's interesting, it's chill. I highly recommend give it a shot since it's 4 hours long. I've checked just now.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight a one-hit-kill mechanic where both the player character and standard enemies die instantly from a single attack.

citations.review_text:
“Guys, I have this neat, ridiculous idea. How ‘bout we make game where everyone die from one hit”
“What do you mean >>Everyone<<, boss?”
“EEEEEEVERYOOOOOONE!!!!!”

And this is the basic premise of Katana Zero. Your character, as well as all enemies — well, aside bosses — die from one attack. There are no health bars, no damage calculation, no armor to protect you. When the hit connects with you, you are dead. If you think now “cool, just in Hotline Miami” then yes, you are correct. Also, just like in that game, you must clear areas in one go, checkpoints are only when you travel to the next screen. Thankfully levels are small, so you can waste a minute or two on repeating sections (well, at least on normal difficulty…). What is different is perspective — here we have a normal 2D platformer, instead of a top-down view from above… You also cannot use guns or other weapons, just your trusty swords. To protect yourself you can dodge, reflect bullets — but this one is on the cooldown — and slow down time, which is a godsend, because 80% of enemies in this game use firearms. Your objective in every level is very simple:

Kill. All. Bad. Guys. 
Slaughter. Them. One. By. One.

You are this one cool ninja-samurai guy, pumped on some kind of war drug that allows you to see the future and slow time. So from a story perspective gameplay is not about actual fighting, but about planning all your moves in advance and executing them in the background. It doesn't change anything when playing, but it's a neat idea, connecting lore to players’ agenda. Overall I find the story in this game pretty intriguing — and well executed — and surprisingly deep, at least for a mechanical, challenge oriented game (because compared to more story oriented titles, it's nothing special)… but it’s unfinished. It feels more like a prologue to something bigger, it creates a solid foundation, but leaves players without a proper payout and execution. And considering how long the DLC — yeah, only D…

The game Katana ZERO is renowned for its crisp combat mechanics and extremely low tolerance for error. It also features an incredible soundtrack that complements its theme, blending cyberpunk with a vaporwave vibe. The plot is concise yet tragic. At first, when playing as Zero, I thought he was a veteran soldier who suffered memory loss due to combat injuries, trapped in memories of his childhood and haunted by nightmares every night. As the missions progressed, I gradually learned that the protagonist is a super-soldier who injects a special drug to foresee the future, choosing the best method to eliminate enemies from numerous possibilities. Every time the protagonist returns home, a little girl is waiting for him. After becoming familiar, Zero even invites her to his home. However, there is a strange detail: the doll the little girl is looking for bears some resemblance to Zero's memories. During missions, Zero slowly uncovers the side effects of the drug and learns that there are other super-soldiers like him, such as the most intimidating Dragon King. Later, I had the chance to play as him. After completing his final mission, he seems to recall his past—he is not the child but the one who eliminated the child. Dragon King was his teammate, and the little girl from earlier is also a victim (killed alongside the little boy). This is likely the side effect of the drug. The game also has a bad ending, and I am looking forward to the release of the new DLC.
